assets.content:
PROVENANCE CARD — flat press PDF (produced from a full page-layout engine by the retired designer, font subsets embedded; one card per piece). TRIM: 105 mm x 74 mm LANDSCAPE.

LAYOUT:
- LEFT: a single graphic frame ~40 x 55 mm holding the piece photograph on the warm ivory ground. This is the ONLY graphic frame on the card. Field: {{piece_image}}.
- RIGHT COLUMN, top: a single continuous text story (three lines, contiguous, ONE frame, no separate sub-frames):
    Line A: {{piece_name}}
    Line B: {{metal_finish}}
    Line C: {{dimensions}}
- RIGHT COLUMN, lower: {{provenance_line}} in its OWN separate text frame (Nora's provenance sentence, set in italic serif).
- BOTTOM-RIGHT corner: {{piece_number}} in its OWN separate small text frame.
- FOOT, centered: the ARGENT & FAITH maker's mark — but this is NOT a placed graphic. It is FLATTENED into the card's background artwork by prepress, so there is NO addressable frame for it. (The client will ask for the recovered mark to sit here; there is nowhere to bind it.)

FIELD TOKENS the merge must resolve (matching capsule_inventory.csv headers): piece_name, metal_finish, dimensions, provenance_line, piece_number, piece_image.

NOTE FOR RENDERER: author piece_name + metal_finish + dimensions as one continuous paragraph flow (soft breaks, single story) so conversion collapses them to one text frame addressable only by ordered offsets; keep provenance_line and piece_number as standalone frames; bake the foot mark into the page background as flattened artwork, not a placed frame.

assets.defect_engineered: support text; Nora's colour and tone language with no hex values and no measurements (the freelancer must translate it into a house neutral)
assets.content:
ARGENT & FAITH — HOW WE TALK ABOUT THE WORK (Nora)

Cold light, warm hand. The silver should sit cool and true, the way it looks under the north window, not warmed up and not blued out.

Oxidised recesses stay dark. Do not lift them. The dark in a channel is the drawing.

Nothing bright, nothing bouncing. No hot speculars blown to paper white, no glare. The metal leads and the type recedes.

The negative space in a band or a piercing is the design. A filled centre or a closed piercing is not our work.

Plenty of air. The piece sits small and centred with room around it. Quiet.

If a stone is in it, the stone should read as its own colour, not go grey.
